key_path: Sign up at msg91.com with email + mobile number. Verify the mobile via OTP and verify email
Log in to the MSG91 panel > Authkey (top bar)
Re-verify the registered mobile number with OTP to access the Authkey section
Create New: name it, pick 'Where are you integrating', attach a Rule (service-scoped permissions), whitelist IPs (IP security is ON by default)
Add balance / buy credits for real sends; a small free trial credit is typical

For SMS to Indian numbers: complete TRAI DLT registration (Principal Entity ID on an operator DLT portal, header/sender ID and template approval) and map DLT template IDs in MSG91 before production SMS. WhatsApp needs Meta Business verification
human_gates_notes: Phone OTP is needed both at signup AND again to view/create authkeys. DLT (TRAI TCCCPR) registration is mandatory for Indian commercial SMS, and templates are approved by telcos. 'credit_card_required' here means prepaid balance for live traffic.

agent_native_auth.scoped_keys: yes. Authkey Rules restrict a key to selected services, plus an IP whitelist

mcp.notes: No official MSG91 MCP found (docs.msg91.com/mcp 404; mcp.msg91.com does not resolve to a service). Third-party wrappers exist via Composio and n8n.

docs_for_agents.llms_txt: yes but weak. https://docs.msg91.com/llms.txt has ~144 endpoint links with EMPTY descriptions, titled 'LLM Usage Policy'
docs_for_agents.markdown_pages: no (.md returns 404; docs are a Next.js app on techdoc.walkover.in)

score_justification: Scoped, IP-locked authkeys are good hygiene, but OTP walls (twice), DLT registration, no MCP and an llms.txt with no descriptions make it hard for agents.
best_practice: Rule-scoped authkeys with an IP whitelist on by default, which limits the blast radius of an agent-held key
biggest_gap: Phone-OTP re-verification just to view or create a key, and a stub llms.txt with no descriptions or markdown pages
